title: Tanganyika Independence
note: December 9 1961 confirmed; Nyerere as PM confirmed; TANU won 70/71 seats in 1960 confirmed.

title: Tanganyika Becomes a Republic
note: December 9 1962 republic date confirmed; Nyerere elected first president confirmed.

title: Zanzibar Achieves Independence
note: December 10 1963 confirmed (event says 'December 10' implicitly); constitutional monarchy under Sultan Jamshid confirmed.

title: Zanzibar Revolution
note: January 12 1964 confirmed; Karume became president confirmed. Minor note: revolution was physically led by John Okello, not ASP directly, but Karume/ASP took power — description is broadly accurate.

title: Tanganyika and Zanzibar Unite to Form Tanzania
note: April 26 1964 confirmed; Nyerere president, Karume first VP confirmed; autonomous Zanzibar institutions confirmed.

title: One-Party State Established
note: 1965 one-party bill confirmed; opposition abolished confirmed; persists until 1992 confirmed.

title: Arusha Declaration — Ujamaa African Socialism
note: February 5 1967 confirmed; nationalization of banks, industries, sisal plantations confirmed; leadership code confirmed.

title: East African Community Established
note: Treaty signed June 1967, came into force December 1 1967 confirmed; Tanzania, Kenya, Uganda confirmed.

title: Ujamaa Villagization Campaigns Begin
note: Scale of ~11 million people confirmed (7M by June 1975, then 4M more). Voluntary-to-coercive shift confirmed. Year 1971 for start is slightly early — compulsory phase began 1972/73 — but voluntary campaigns did begin earlier; broadly accurate.

title: Zanzibar's President Karume Assassinated
note: April 7 1972 confirmed; assassinated at ASP headquarters confirmed; Umma Party connection confirmed.

title: Capital Moved from Dar es Salaam to Dodoma
note: October 1973 announcement by Nyerere confirmed; partial/slow transfer confirmed; Dar es Salaam retaining de facto status confirmed.

title: Forced Villagization — Operation Sogeza
note: Operation Sogeza/Vijiji confirmed; burning of homesteads, military escorts confirmed; 1975 peak phase confirmed.

title: TANU and ASP Merge to Form CCM
note: February 5 1977 confirmed; TANU + ASP merger confirmed; CCM monopoly until 1992 confirmed.

title: East African Community Collapses
note: 1977 dissolution confirmed; ideological/financial disputes Tanzania-Kenya confirmed; border closure confirmed.

title: Uganda Invades Tanzania — Kagera Region Annexed
note: October 1978 invasion confirmed; 1,800 sq km Kagera Salient annexed confirmed; ~1,500 civilian deaths confirmed.

title: Tanzania Invades Uganda — Idi Amin Ousted
note: Kampala captured April 11 1979 confirmed; Amin fled into exile confirmed. Specific figure of 45,000 troops not confirmed in sources, but substantial Tanzanian force with UNLA allies confirmed.

title: Tanzania-Uganda War Causes Economic Crisis
note: War cost estimates in $500M–$1B range are cited in academic literature; combined with Ujamaa failures and oil shocks causing major debt crisis confirmed.

title: IMF Negotiations Break Down — Austerity Rejected
note: IMF standby loan negotiations failed 1979-1981 confirmed; Nyerere rejection of devaluation/liberalization confirmed; NESP 1981 as alternative confirmed.

title: Zanzibar Autonomy Tensions — Jumbe Pressures Union
note: Jumbe pushed for three-tier structure confirmed; forced resignation January 1984 confirmed. Year given as 1982 for onset of tensions is reasonable though resignation was 1984.

title: Economic Reform Program Launched
note: NESP and Economic Recovery Programme confirmed; partial retreat from Ujamaa without full SAP confirmed; 1984/85 launch confirmed.

title: Nyerere Voluntarily Hands Over Power to Mwinyi
note: November 5 1985 Mwinyi sworn in confirmed; Nyerere retained CCM chairmanship until 1990 confirmed; voluntary retirement confirmed.

title: Structural Adjustment Agreement with IMF
note: 1986 stand-by agreement confirmed; currency devaluation, trade liberalization, price control removal confirmed.

title: AIDS Epidemic Devastates Tanzania
note: 1988 second-highest HIV prevalence in Africa on TANZAM road confirmed; Lake Victoria corridor severely hit confirmed; truck-route transmission confirmed.

title: Nyerere Calls for Multiparty Democracy
note: February 1990 Nyerere acknowledged one-party failure confirmed; 'no longer treasonable to discuss multiparty' confirmed.

title: Multiparty Constitution Adopted
note: Constitutional amendment July 1992, Political Parties Act May 1992 confirmed; 27 years one-party rule (1965-1992) confirmed.

title: Zanzibar Multiparty Crisis — Union Stability Threatened
note: CUF registered January 21 1993 confirmed; Muslim/opposition support base confirmed; recurring election violence 1995-2005 confirmed.

title: Rwandan Genocide — Tanzania Hosts 500,000 Refugees
note: ~580,000 Rwandan refugees to Tanzania confirmed (event says ~500,000 — slightly low but in range). Fastest mass movement claim confirmed. Environmental damage in Kagera/Kigoma region confirmed.

title: First Multiparty Elections — Mkapa Wins Presidency
note: October 29 1995 election confirmed; Mkapa won 61.8% confirmed; Zanzibar irregularities confirmed.

title: Zanzibar Election Violence — CUF Rejects Results
note: CCM won Zanzibar by <1% margin confirmed; CUF refused to recognize results confirmed; CUF boycotted parliament confirmed; pattern recurring 2000/2005 confirmed.

title: US Embassy Bombing in Dar es Salaam
note: August 7 1998 confirmed; 11 killed in Dar es Salaam confirmed; 85 injured confirmed; al-Qaeda confirmed.

title: Nyerere Dies — Founder's Legacy Secured
note: October 14 1999 confirmed; leukemia confirmed; died in London confirmed.

title: Zanzibar Election Massacre — Pemba Killings
note: At least 35 CUF supporters killed confirmed (HRW). Date note: killings occurred January 27 2001 (post-October 2000 election) — event year listed as 2000 refers to the disputed election, killings were 2001. Core claim verified.

title: Muafaka Accord — Zanzibar Power-Sharing
note: Muafaka signed October 10 2001 confirmed; CCM-CUF accord confirmed; implementation confirmed ~80% by end 2003.

title: Kikwete Wins Presidency — New Generation Leader
note: Kikwete won 80.28% confirmed (event says 'approximately 80%'); largest popular margin confirmed; December 14 2005 election confirmed.

title: Zanzibar Electoral Reforms — Reduced Violence
note: Muafaka reforms improved 2005 conditions vs 2000 confirmed; CCM maintained power confirmed.

title: Tanzania Natural Gas Discoveries
note: 2008 onshore Ruvuma gas discovery confirmed. Largest offshore finds were 2010-2014 (47 TCF); event description referring to 2008 as start of major discoveries is accurate for onshore — slightly imprecise on offshore timing.

title: Zanzibar Government of National Unity
note: July 31 2010 referendum confirmed; GNU with CUF ministerial positions confirmed; most significant stability advance confirmed.

title: Sectarian Violence in Zanzibar
note: Acid attacks on Christian clergy 2012-2013 confirmed; Muslim-Christian clashes confirmed; Uamsho group confirmed; heavy-handed policing confirmed.

title: Kisutu Courthouse Bombing — Dar es Salaam
note: Could not confirm a specific Kisutu courthouse bomb in May 2013. General Islamist terrorism in Tanzania 2013-2014 is confirmed (Uamsho, church bombings, St. Joseph Arusha). The specific Kisutu courthouse incident is not corroborated by available sources.

title: LNG Plant Negotiations — $30 Billion Investment Stalls
note: $30B figure confirmed for 2014; Statoil, BG Group, ExxonMobil consortium confirmed; stalled negotiations confirmed; fiscal terms/local content disputes confirmed.

title: Magufuli Wins Election — Authoritarian Populist Shift
note: Magufuli 58.46% confirmed; Lowassa/Chadema opponent confirmed; opposition fraud allegations confirmed; authoritarian turn confirmed.

title: Magufuli Launches Sweeping Anti-Corruption Drive
note: Port revenue fraud uncovered confirmed; worker dismissals confirmed; ghost workers purge confirmed; initial popular enthusiasm confirmed.

title: Media Crackdowns and Opposition Repression Begin
note: Newspaper suspensions, live broadcast bans, journalist/politician arrests confirmed from 2016 onward.

title: Opposition Activity Banned — Rallies and Meetings Prohibited
note: Ban imposed 2016/2017 confirmed (6-year ban lifted January 2023 confirms it started ~2016-2017); applied only to opposition in practice confirmed.

title: EACOP Pipeline Agreement Signed
note: May 2017 IGA confirmed; 1,443 km confirmed; Hoima to Tanga port confirmed; TotalEnergies lead investor confirmed; environmental controversy confirmed.

title: Magufuli Withdraws from EAC Economic Partnership Agreement
note: Magufuli refused to sign EU-EAC EPA confirmed; 'form of colonialism' language confirmed; EAC partners tension confirmed. Refusal began ~2016-2017 not strictly 2018, but the stance was maintained and formalized through 2018.

title: Homosexuality Crackdown — Dar es Salaam Arrests
note: October 2018 Makonda task force announced confirmed; HIV NGO shutdowns confirmed; dozens arrested confirmed; international health warnings confirmed.

title: MV Bukoba Ferry Sinking — 228 Dead
note: The 2018 ferry disaster involved MV Nyerere (not MV Bukoba). MV Nyerere capsized September 20 2018 on Lake Victoria with official death toll of 228 confirmed. MV Bukoba is a 1996 disaster (~894 dead). The year, death toll, lake, and Magufuli response are all correct — only the ship name is wrong.

title: Dodoma Becomes Formal Capital
note: Magufuli completed government relocation to Dodoma by end 2019 confirmed; Dar es Salaam remaining commercial center confirmed. Note: National Assembly had already moved to Dodoma in 1996, not 2019 — but the 2019 executive relocation is confirmed.

title: Tanzania 2020 Elections — Opposition Decimated
note: Official result ~84-85% for Magufuli confirmed; opposition fraud/suppression allegations confirmed; at least 7 killed confirmed; international observers denied access confirmed; Lissu in exile confirmed.

title: Magufuli Denies COVID-19 — Promotes Herbal Cures
note: COVID denial confirmed; herbal remedies/prayer promotion confirmed; data reporting stopped May 2020 confirmed; no lockdown confirmed.

title: Magufuli Dies — Samia Hassan Becomes First Female President
note: March 17 2021 Magufuli death confirmed; officially heart failure confirmed; Hassan sworn in March 19 2021 confirmed; first female president in East Africa confirmed.

title: Hassan Reverses Magufuli's COVID Denialism
note: Rapid reversal confirmed; mask campaign, WHO data reporting, vaccine acceptance confirmed; pragmatic contrast with Magufuli confirmed.

title: EACOP Final Investment Decision Approaches
note: February 2021 FID signed confirmed; TotalEnergies and CNOOC confirmed; European bank withdrawals confirmed; ESG controversy confirmed.

title: Hassan Opens Political Space — Opposition Rallies Permitted
note: Newspaper bans lifted February 2022 confirmed; Freeman Mbowe released March 2022 confirmed. Note: rally ban formally lifted January 3 2023 (not 2022) — but the broader political opening started in 2022 with newspaper/prisoner releases.

title: Tanzania Rejoins EAC Economic Partnership Talks
note: Tanzania changed stance and agreed to EPA engagement under Hassan confirmed; reversal of Magufuli's trade isolationism confirmed.

title: Zanzibar Separatist Tensions Resurface
note: ACT-Wazalendo autonomy demands confirmed; union grievances and economic disparities confirmed; tourism-driven new political dynamics confirmed.

title: EACOP Construction Controversy Intensifies
note: Displacement of Tanzanian households without adequate compensation confirmed; harassment of communities and activists confirmed; TotalEnergies pressing ahead with alternative financing confirmed; ESG debate confirmed.

title: Constitutional Review Process Launched
note: May 2023 Hassan directed constitutional review process confirmed; Zanzibar union question as most sensitive issue confirmed. Note: Hassan then stalled process in September 2023 citing 'insufficient time' — so launch confirmed but outcome uncertain.

title: Tanzania Joins African Continental Free Trade Area
note: Tanzania ratified AfCFTA on September 9 2021, not 2023. The event year is wrong by 2 years. Ratification itself is confirmed but happened under the transition from Magufuli to Hassan in 2021.

title: Chadema Party Repression Continues
note: August 2024 Chadema mass arrests including Tundu Lissu confirmed; politically motivated charges confirmed; Amnesty International documentation confirmed; pre-2025 election context confirmed.

title: Tanzania Economic Growth — Regional Hub Ambitions
note: 5.5% GDP growth 2024 confirmed; infrastructure investment, tourism expansion confirmed; Dar es Salaam port modernization and EACOP transit corridor positioning confirmed.
